note: Groups are the 127 g-percentiles of Gethin & Fisher-Post (2026), "Government Redistribution and Global Poverty Reduction", data version 2026-09-22: all individuals, with income split equally within couples (WID's 999j unit), ranked by pretax national income. Sizes and average incomes are theirs.

Amounts are in national currency at 2023 prices: Gethin-Fisher values (PPP USD of 2024) times defl (0.928371) times xppp_us (456.078). Their ReadMe gives the PPP base year as 2023, but xppp_us matches WID's 2024 PPP, so we take the base to be 2024.
Check: total pretax income from Gethin-Fisher is 0.961 times WID's national income for 2023.

Lower thresholds come from WID's tptinc999j for 2023, made nominal and scaled by each group's ratio of Gethin-Fisher's to WID's average income (108 of 126 groups; 18 unscaled where that ratio was unavailable or outside 0.5-2). The bottom group's threshold is set to 0, since Gethin-Fisher's averages don't follow WID's negative incomes.
29 thresholds fell outside the averages of the groups on either side and were moved to the nearer one: p1p2 p2p3 p3p4 p4p5 p5p6 p6p7 p7p8 p8p9 p9p10 p10p11 p11p12 p12p13 ….

The current income tax rate by group (effectiveIncomeTaxShareOfIncome) is Gethin-Fisher's personal income tax (tax_dir_pit, their central estimate) over pretax income. Their lower and upper bounds aren't used.
Data quality Modeled, from WID's data-quality score of 2 (out of 5) on the income thresholds: 4 or 5 is Credible, lower is Modeled.

paramIndividualIncomeTaxCalibratedBaseShareOfIncome (λ): each individual's pretax national income is scaled by λ before the current income tax schedule is applied, with λ chosen so the schedule reproduces Gethin-Fisher's total personal income tax (tax_dir_pit). λ absorbs allowances, deductions, credits, preferential rates, filing-unit effects and evasion, so it is not a measured taxable-income share.

The calibration applies the schedule to group excess curves built from the groups fixture: exact below each group's lower threshold, the midpoint of the upper and lower bounds within a group, and a Pareto tail in the top group (α = a/(a − m)). The model must build its curves the same way to reproduce the target. Target: income tax of 2.83% of pretax income; the schedule applied to all pretax income would raise 11.21%.
OECD Revenue Statistics: personal income tax (code 1100) was 1.92% of GDP in 2023 (central government 1.92%).

Central government: the 2023 statutory schedule from the OECD Tax Database, "Personal income tax (PIT) - central government rates and thresholds" (SDMX dataflow OECD.CTP.TPS,DSD_TAX_PIT@DF_PIT_CENT), for a single person without dependents, applied to wage income. Thresholds are in national currency, nominal 2023. The OECD reports each bracket's upper limit; we store lower limits, starting at 0. 8 brackets, from 0% to a top rate of 40% above 235,572,720.
The first bracket, up to 10,258,812, has a zero rate: a tax-free band built into the schedule.
The OECD's sub-central income tax tables have no entry for this country in 2023, so the schedule is the central government's alone.
Capital income (dividends, capital gains, interest) may be taxed under separate rules, e.g. at flat or preferential rates; the general model applies this schedule only.
